item.title: [ecmascript] Question: Could one here use `transfer()` to release the previous ArrayBuffer?
item.content:encoded:
MDN URL

https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/GPUBuffer

What specific section or headline is this issue about?

About the .slice(0) in the code snippet

What information was incorrect, unhelpful, or incomplete?

The code in the website is:

// map staging buffer to read results back to JS
await stagingBuffer.mapAsync(
  GPUMapMode.READ,
  0, // Offset
  BUFFER_SIZE, // Length
);

const copyArrayBuffer = stagingBuffer.getMappedRange(0, BUFFER_SIZE);
const data = copyArrayBuffer.slice(0);
stagingBuffer.unmap();
console.log(new Float32Array(data));

What did you expect to see?

I am wondering whether .transfer() isn't more useful (although I understand that this is a relatively new feature.)

I'd be unsure whether in this case we need .unmap though since:

When unmap() is called, any ArrayBuffers created via GPUBuffer.getMappedRange() are detached.

may end up erroring?

Do you have any supporting links, references, or citations?

No response

Do you have anything more you want to share?

I'd appreciate any help understanding this case since I find the interaction between arraybuffers and gpu buffers a little bit confusing up to now.

item.title: [streams, ecmascript] ReadableStreamDefaultController: undocumented error conditions
item.content:encoded:
MDN URL

https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/ReadableStreamDefaultController/close

What specific section or headline is this issue about?

Exceptions

What information was incorrect, unhelpful, or incomplete?

The "Exceptions" section says:

TypeError
Thrown if the source object is not a ReadableStreamDefaultController.

This suggests that errors are not thrown in other cases.

What did you expect to see?

I expect to see that a TypeError may be thrown by this method if the stream is already in the process of closing or closed.

Do you have any supporting links, references, or citations?

https://streams.spec.whatwg.org/#rs-default-controller-close

Do you have anything more you want to share?

Similar issues exist for ReadableStreamDefaultController.enqueue and probably methods on WritableStreamDefaultController as well.
